name: fprobe
why: A libpcap-based NetFlow probe; a door into flow telemetry that most people never see, though it's fairly utilitarian.

brief.what_it_is: fprobe is a NetFlow probe: a daemon that captures network traffic using libpcap and emits it as NetFlow flows to a collector you specify. Its SourceForge description says it 'collect[s] network traffic data and emit[s] it as NetFlow flows towards the specified collector.' The input is live packet capture on a network interface, and the output is NetFlow records sent to a collector. The same listing also describes a sibling, fprobe-ulog, as a libipulog-based fork of fprobe. The homepage lists it as Linux and BSD, written in C, and non-interactive.
brief.why_it_exists: The SourceForge listing gives no stated motivation beyond describing the tool itself. It serves as a traffic-flow exporter, feeding NetFlow collectors and analysers when a router cannot export NetFlow itself.
brief.how_it_works: The probe uses libpcap to capture packets on an interface, aggregates them into flows, and exports those flows as NetFlow records to a specified collector host. The homepage does not describe the flow-expiry or record-format details.
brief.install_notes: The homepage gives no install steps, configuration, or command-line usage. The listed platforms are BSD and Linux. It is a C program under GPLv2, so building it from source is the likely route, but I did not see build instructions. The one file-download link was not followed, so I cannot confirm package contents.
brief.standout: It is a small, focused flow exporter that turns raw packet capture into NetFlow for any collector, so it can sit on a box with no native flow support. The homepage also lists a libipulog-based sibling, fprobe-ulog, which points to a fork with a different capture backend.
brief.status: quiet. The SourceForge page shows Last Update 2013-04-22 and a project registration date of 2002-09-27. The listing shows 10 downloads this week and two reviews. I found no newer release or commit on the page, so I cannot call it actively maintained.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a SourceForge landing page with no README or documentation in the text I could read. The last recorded update is from 2013, so it may not build or run cleanly on current systems. Platforms are listed as BSD and Linux only. The licence is GPLv2. The description is brief, and I could not find a usage guide.
quotes: fprobe - libpcap-based tool that collect network traffic data and emit it as NetFlow flows towards the specified collector.
fetch_log: https://sourceforge.net/projects/fprobe/ - fetched and returned the SourceForge project page, with the description, license, platforms, and review text. It contained no README or documentation. I did not follow the 'fprobe Web Site' link because its URL was not present in the text.
